paper_title: OmniStepBench: Deployment-Aware Agent Evaluation across Modalities and Task Complexity
reason: OmniStepBench는 22개 원본 벤치마크에서 233개 과제를 골라 만든 재사용 가능한 에이전트 벤치마크로 보이며, 영어 과제 예시가 있어 en 트랙 후보입니다. 하지만 PDF 어디에도 이 벤치마크의 공식 데이터셋이나 코드 URL이 나오지 않습니다. 본문에 적힌 URL은 OpenClaw 런타임과 다른 벤치마크(WildClawBench)의 것이며, 보충 자료는 언급만 있고 주소가 없습니다. 링크 근거를 확보할 수 없으므로 행을 제안하지 않고 추가 증거를 요청합니다.

screening.paper_title: OmniStepBench: Deployment-Aware Agent Evaluation across Modalities and Task Complexity
screening.abstract: As large language models evolve from question-answering systems into general-purpose agents, evaluation must move beyond static answer correctness to assess multimodal perception, multi-step execution, tool use, and artifact delivery. However, existing benchmarks are often tied to specific task types, execution environments, or scoring protocols, limiting their comparability, interpretability, and reliability for deployment decisions. We introduce \textbf{OmniStepBench}, a benchmark for deployment-aware agent evaluation across modalities and task complexity. Built on a shared OpenClaw execution environment, OmniStepBench organizes 233 tasks selected and adapted from 22 source benchmarks into a $2\times3$ workload matrix defined by input modality and execution form, and evaluates them under a unified contract-based protocol with evidence-based score auditing. We evaluate 30 commercial API models and 12 locally deployed open-weight models (42 models in total) over 9{,}218 applicable model--task runs, reporting accuracy and token consumption alongside reference costs for API models. Results show workload-dependent rankings, distinct accuracy--cost trade-offs between text and multimodal tasks, and competitive but weaker overall performance from local models. These findings support deployment decisions based on workload profiles, deployment mode, and accuracy--cost trade-offs rather than a single aggregate score.
